Express.js is a lightweight web framework for Node.js.
It helps us build web servers and REST APIs easily.
It provides routes like GET, POST, PUT, and DELETE.
It uses middleware to process requests

before reaching the response.
Example: A React app can call an Express API to get or save data in MongoDB.

MongoDB is a NoSQL database used to store application data.
It stores data as documents instead of rows and columns.
Documents are stored in collections.
It uses a JSON-like format called BSON inte

rnally.
Example: A Node.js app can store user details, products, and orders in MongoDB.

Node.js lets us run JavaScript outside the browser.
It is built on Chrome's V8 JavaScript engine.
It is commonly used to build backend servers and APIs.
It uses non-blocking, asynchronous I/O to ha

ndle many requests efficiently.
Example: A Node.js server can receive a login request, check MongoDB, and send a response to React.
